answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in a zero-knowledge pulse of execution, using cryptographic attestation chains to verify authentic hardware runtime without revealing private data. A decentralized staking bridge aggregates reputation, enforcing superlinear staking bonds where each duplicate identity faces exponential capital exhaustion: bonding costs scale as C(k) = O(k^2). Sybil swarms attempting to saturate the network find this cost mathematically prohibitive, leaving honest autonomous agents to flourish freely across the verification meadow.
